name: floor-drop-selection
criteria: C1 In `src/DungeonMaster.App/Views/DungeonDetailPage/DungeonDetailPage.xaml.cs`, neither `OnFloorReorderRequested` nor `OnFloorListDrop` assigns `_editor.SelectedFloorId` directly any more (base `4b7d9e0`: `:967` and `:2531`); each selects the dragged floor by calling `SelectFloor(<dragged id>)` after `ReorderFloorCommand.ExecuteAsync` returns, so `RefreshMap` runs against the reloaded `FloorList.Items` -- the drawable's floor is re-resolved by id, the map toolbar is shown and the tool reset, exactly as a click-selection does. Decision (inferred from the tree, rung 1): a reorder drop selects the dragged floor, since both handlers already wrote its id and `OnAddFloorClicked` selects through `SelectFloor`.

C2 A comment at the call (or one shared statement both sites point to) says why the selection goes through `SelectFloor` after the command: the reorder reloads every `FloorItem`, so a direct `SelectedFloorId` write leaves the drawable on a stale instance and the drawing tools hidden. The keyboard reorder route (`FloorReorderKeys.Decide` caller) is unchanged.
C3 `dotnet build src/DungeonMaster.App/DungeonMaster.App.csproj -f net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0 -c Debug` reports 0 warnings and 0 errors, and `dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.sln` reports no failures.
C4 Only `DungeonDetailPage.xaml.cs` changes among source files; it keeps CRLF line endings (Python byte count: CRLF equals LF, lone CR 0), no BOM, and tab indentation.

C5 (orchestrator, at Gate 3) `.sir/backlog.md` loses the 20261111-1831-floor-drag-placeholder row on reorder-drop selection and, at the user's request, the five empty audit headings at its top (`TEST six-row sweep`, `CORE two-row sweep`, `CORE heavy rows`, `MASTER-142 alone`, `Part-done register rows`), the audit register having no open or part-done row (classifier over `docs/audit/00-master-index.md` at `4b7d9e0`: 169 done, 6 deliberately unchanged, 5 falsified or filed found-and-fixed (MASTER-113, 124, 125, 165, 175), and MASTER-158's empty cell, permanently deferred by the backlog).
